tasks.short: Prepare claim documents, check completeness and obtain missing information.

steps.what: Retrieve claim documents and the policy record from the insurance case system.
Read supporting documents and enter facts into the insurance case system.

loop.input: Unstructured claim documents; structured submissions bypass the model.
loop.output: Claim fields with document references and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate field types, policy identifiers and dates; show source passages for clerk review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved fields return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms and mappings handle structured inputs; varied narratives and attachments still require reading.

steps.what: Prepare the claim form and supporting document list.
Check required fields, signatures and consistency against the policy record.
Contact the policyholder about missing facts and record their explanation.
Save the completed claim pack and pass it to the claims handler.

tasks.design: Configure the insurance case system in {OTHER} to retrieve records, populate forms in {DOCS}, check required evidence and route completed packs. A bounded extractor on {DATA_PLATFORM} handles varied attachments, with field review before posting; the clerk receives a missing-information checklist for policyholder conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document formats varied, required evidence differed by claim type, and records were poorly connected.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing form builders and validation rules cover much of the work. Bounded extraction handles remaining documents, while AI-assisted coding can shorten connector development.
tasks.still_hard: Missing evidence, contradictory accounts and unusual policy wording remain difficult. GDPR requires controlled access and a lawful basis, including applicable conditions for health data.
tasks.human_edge: Help distressed policyholders explain events and distinguish an absent document from an unclear account.

ambition.what: Assisted claim completion appointments for policyholders who struggle with digital forms

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time copying facts and more time resolving incomplete claims. They gain authority to offer assisted completion appointments within agreed service limits, not to decide coverage.

reach.task: Design an accessible document intake checklist.
reach.learn: Plain-language forms, alternative submission routes and document accessibility.

evidence.claim: Paperbox organises insurance emails and attachments into case files.
VKG has a documented case automating claims correspondence; it does not establish this task's savings.
Templates, required-field rules and a bounded extractor can support claim-pack preparation.

assumptions: The company processes insurance claims using an insurance case system represented by {OTHER}.
Shares and remaining-time estimates describe a typical task mix, not measured savings.
Document-heavy priors fit this task; clarification calls take more time than the weak mail prior suggests.
Build ranges cover a narrow pilot and may overlap; national consultation requirements vary.
unknowns: Claim types, required evidence and document languages.
Available templates, validation features and read/write access in {OTHER}.
Proportion of structured submissions and incomplete claims.
Applicable national rules, employee consultation requirements and health-data access conditions.
research_questions: Which completeness checks can existing configuration handle?
How accurately can extraction preserve facts and flag contradictions on representative documents?
new_work: Review extracted fields and unresolved completeness checks.
Maintain claim templates and evidence requirements.
Monitor access controls, extraction errors and connector failures.

tasks.short: Calculate a proposed claim amount from evidence and policy terms.

steps.what: Retrieve the claim pack and policy terms from the insurance case system.
Read estimates and invoices, then enter loss amounts into the insurance case system.

loop.input: Repair estimates, supplier invoices and other loss evidence.
loop.output: Itemised amounts, currencies, tax fields and source references.
loop.check: Reconcile line items to totals; check duplicates, currencies and claim identifiers; review ambiguous amounts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; failed reconciliation returns to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured feeds use mappings; varied estimates and scanned evidence need document reading.

steps.what: Apply policy limits, deductibles and valuation rules to calculate the proposed amount.
Resolve disputed valuation or unclear policy treatment with the claims handler.
Record the calculation and its supporting explanation in the insurance case system.

tasks.design: Configure versioned calculation rules in the insurance case system in {OTHER}, using verified loss amounts and policy terms. A bounded extractor on {DATA_PLATFORM} reads residual documents from {DOCS}; unclear valuation goes to a claims handler, and the calculation remains a proposal until settlement approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Amounts arrived in documents, policy versions were difficult to map, and calculation tools did not explain exceptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calculation engines and validation rules already handle arithmetic. Better document extraction and faster connector development can close input gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Depreciation, causation, disputed repair scope and unusual policy terms need expertise. GDPR Article 22 conditions must be assessed before any solely automated decision with significant effects; this design does not automate refusals.
tasks.human_edge: Explain a disputed valuation and recognise when a technically correct formula gives an unsupported result.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of valuation exceptions by financial exposure and claimant delay

tasks.altitude: Routine arithmetic leaves the clerk's queue, while handlers spend more time on disputed evidence. The clerk can prioritise valuation referrals within agreed limits; settlement authority does not change.

reach.task: Analyse recurring valuation exceptions and propose rule improvements.
reach.learn: Exception sampling, financial exposure analysis and policy-version comparison.

evidence.claim: Shift Claims supports claims triage and automation of claims or parts of claims.
A documented motor-claims case automates eligible claims under restricted conditions; it does not establish general valuation coverage.
Claim arithmetic can use deterministic rules while disputed valuation remains with a handler.

assumptions: Routine calculations use {OTHER}; local spreadsheet workarounds are possible but not assumed.
The handler step represents exception time averaged across the task mix.
The judgement prior concerns valuation and policy interpretation, not arithmetic.
Estimates exclude rebuilding a full policy calculation engine; national consultation requirements vary.
unknowns: Existing calculation features and completeness of versioned policy rules.
Claim mix, valuation disputes and settlement authority limits.
Use of spreadsheets for unusual calculations.
Whether life or health pricing enters scope, triggering separate EU AI Act assessment.
research_questions: Which calculations can be configured without custom code?
Can historical cases be replayed with correct policy versions and explainable results?
new_work: Investigate calculation differences and valuation exceptions.
Check rule changes against representative historical claims.

tasks.short: Match incoming information to a claim and attach it to the case file.

steps.what: Open incoming claim correspondence and download attachments from the shared mailbox.
Find the matching claim in the insurance case system.

loop.input: Correspondence without a valid structured claim reference.
loop.output: Candidate claim identifiers with source passages.
loop.check: Use exact references first; corroborate extracted identifiers against case records; never match by name alone.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt; multiple or uncorroborated matches enter a clerk queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact matching handles most references; identifiers embedded in free text require reading.

steps.what: Identify document type and check whether the file already exists.

loop.output: An allowed document category or unknown.
loop.check: Validate against the category list; compute exact duplicate hashes deterministically; preserve changed versions.
loop.stop: One classification attempt; unknown categories return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender rules and metadata cover standard documents; varied correspondence lacks consistent labels.

steps.what: Upload documents and metadata to the insurance case file.
Notify the claims handler that new evidence is available.

tasks.design: Connect {EMAIL} directly to the insurance case system in {OTHER} and {DOCS}, removing manual downloads and uploads. Exact identifiers and duplicate checks run first; bounded extraction and classification handle residual documents, while ambiguous matches wait for clerk resolution before attachment.
tasks.previous_blocker: The mailbox and case file were separate, references were inconsistent, and duplicate handling was weak.
tasks.enabler_now: Mailbox ingestion, case-system configuration and deterministic matching already exist. Small extraction loops can handle references buried in text.
tasks.still_hard: One email can concern several claims, and changed documents can resemble duplicates. Wrong-case attachment exposes personal data, so uncertain matches must remain unposted.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous ownership and understand when a revised document changes the case.

ambition.what: Missing-evidence alerts for claims handlers before scheduled case reviews

tasks.altitude: The clerk works an ambiguity queue instead of moving files. They can correct document categories and case links within access limits, and flag missing evidence for handlers.

reach.task: Improve claim-file indexing and retention categories.
reach.learn: Document versioning, access boundaries and retention schedules.

evidence.claim: Paperbox organises insurance mail and attachments into case files.
VKG documents automation of claims correspondence and improved service-level compliance.
Exact references, duplicate hashes and idempotent attachment writes reduce manual filing.

assumptions: A shared mailbox is a material intake channel, so mail time exceeds the supplied weak prior.
Existing ingestion configuration supports attachments and receipt checks.
Ambiguous matches are resolved before the write step; routine exact matches need no separate approval.
This task shares intake components with claim preparation; savings must not be added twice.
unknowns: Current intake channels and share already attached automatically.
Case-system ingestion features, identifiers and attachment limits.
Frequency of multi-claim correspondence and revised documents.
Retention rules and applicable national employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: What proportion of documents can be matched using exact references alone?
Can attachment retries avoid duplicates while preserving document versions?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous case matches and unknown categories.
Correct attachment mistakes through an audited process.
Maintain sender mappings, category rules and retention settings.
Monitor ingestion failures and missing attachment receipts.

tasks.short: Route approved claims for payment or investigation and confirm receipt.

steps.what: Open the claim pack and calculation in the insurance case system.
Approve settlement or select further investigation within delegated authority.
Prepare the payment instruction or investigation referral packet.
Send approved payment instructions to the finance system.
Send investigation referrals and permitted evidence to the assigned investigator.
Record transmission receipts and chase failed or unacknowledged handoffs.

tasks.design: Configure approval and referral templates in the insurance case system in {OTHER}, then send approved payment requests to {ERP} through a logged, duplicate-safe integration. Investigation referrals use an approved recipient and evidence list through {WORKFLOW}; handlers approve external disclosure, while receipts and timed exception alerts update the case.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approval evidence, payment records and investigation correspondence lived in separate systems, with manual checks for delivery.
tasks.enabler_now: Approval workflows and template generation are established capabilities. Deterministic connectors can carry approval identifiers, prevent duplicate requests and reconcile receipts.
tasks.still_hard: Recipient identity, changed bank details, disclosure scope and delegated authority remain sensitive. GDPR applies to referrals; national rules vary, and actual payment release remains a separate finance action.
tasks.human_edge: Choose proportionate investigation and challenge unsupported suspicion without treating a flag as proof.

ambition.what: Daily escalation of stalled payment and investigation handoffs by claimant impact

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving failed handoffs and less time assembling packets. They gain authority to escalate stalled cases and request missing acknowledgements, while settlement and payment-release rights remain with their current owners.

reach.task: Coordinate investigation milestones and overdue handoffs.
reach.learn: Dependency tracking, escalation thresholds and sensitive-information sharing.

evidence.claim: Shift Claims supports claims triage and automation of parts of the claims process.
DNB's documented 2021 review found flagged claims reaching people in the six insurers reviewed.
Approval-linked requests, duplicate prevention and receipt reconciliation can automate transmission without automating settlement judgement.

assumptions: Payment and investigation are alternative branches; their shares represent an aggregate task mix.
Investigation may involve an external investigator, so disclosure has its own gate.
Sending to {ERP} creates a payment request, not a bank transfer.
Build ranges include access and applicable national consultation; individual productivity monitoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Current settlement limits, approval roles and payment-release controls.
Whether investigators are internal or external and which channels they accept.
Available receipts, retry behaviour and duplicate controls in {ERP} and {OTHER}.
Applicable national consultation requirements and permitted disclosure scope.
research_questions: Can every transmitted request be traced to a valid approval and acknowledged receipt?
Which referral fields and attachments require disclosure review?
new_work: Review external referral recipients and evidence scope.
Resolve failed transmissions and missing acknowledgements.
Maintain authority limits, routing rules and referral templates.
Reconcile payment requests and test duplicate prevention.

role.altitude: The role shifts from copying documents and moving packets to resolving incomplete evidence, ambiguous records and stalled handoffs. Clerks can prioritise exceptions and offer assisted completion; claims handlers retain substantive settlement judgement and finance retains payment release.
reach: File clerk: improve indexing, versioning and retention.
Management analyst: analyse valuation exceptions and financial exposure.
Project management specialist: coordinate investigation dependencies and escalations.
role.ambitious_version: Create a claim completion and handoff service that helps less digitally able policyholders, identifies missing evidence early and escalates delays with a clear audit trail.

job.title: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
